title: NimbleBrain plugin extension
description: The `ai.nimblebrain` entry of an Agent Plugins 1.0 manifest's `extensions` (plugin.json), and of an AI Catalog entry's. It names the plugin's registry servers, its conversation starters, and the contracts it implements and requires. It declares capabilities, never trust: whether a plugin is a system plugin, and where its servers run, are the operator's (nimblebrain.json `plugins`). Other hosts ignore it. Readers ignore fields they do not know.

servers.description: The plugin's servers that have a registry entry: server key to registry name. A key here is the same key as in mcp.json when the plugin also states how to reach the server there; a server only NimbleBrain can reach (a brokered connector) is named here alone. Auth, placements (`ai.nimblebrain/host`) and every other runtime field come from that registry entry's `_meta`, never from this extension.

conversationStarters.description: What a host offers a person who has the plugin and does not know what to ask. Titles are unique within a plugin.

items.description: One conversation starter: something the plugin's tools can do, offered to a person who has the plugin and does not know what to ask.

title.description: The short action a person reads, e.g. "Summarize my unread email".

text.description: What the host sends when the person chooses it.

nimblebrainOnly.description: True when only NimbleBrain can run the plugin: a server it names is brokered, or needs an operator's own OAuth app. A catalog derives it from the servers' auth and states it where it lists the plugin (an AI Catalog entry's `extensions["ai.nimblebrain"]`). It describes the plugin; it grants nothing.

implements.description: The contracts this plugin implements, each at most once. A host binds a contract it consumes when the version meets the one it needs, and ignores a contract it does not consume.

items.description: A contract this plugin implements. Whether several enabled plugins may implement one contract is the contract's own cardinality, never the plugin's.

contract.description: A contract's permanent reverse-DNS id, e.g. "ai.nimblebrain.conversations". Never a URL: where a contract is published is derived from its id.

version.description: The contract version as "major.minor". An implementation at M.m meets a need for N.n when M equals N and m is at least n.

server.description: The key in this plugin's mcp.json `mcpServers` of the one server that implements the contract: it serves the contract's public and private tools. Always an mcp.json key, since mcp.json is where the host learns how to start or reach a server; a server named only by its registry name in `servers` has no address the host can reach at boot. Which tools are private is the contract's decision: the host never offers them to agents, and the server refuses them to any caller but the host.

requires.description: The contracts this plugin uses from other enabled plugins. A requirement no enabled plugin meets refuses the boot unless it is optional.

items.description: A contract (never a plugin) this plugin uses from an enabled plugin that implements it at a compatible version.

contract.description: A contract's permanent reverse-DNS id, e.g. "ai.nimblebrain.conversations". Never a URL: where a contract is published is derived from its id.

version.description: The contract version as "major.minor". An implementation at M.m meets a need for N.n when M equals N and m is at least n.

optional.description: The plugin uses the contract when an enabled plugin implements it, and works without it. Default false: an unmet requirement refuses the boot.
